description.narrative: By supporting women – and promoting dialogue among and between them – the programme will seek to ensure that women change agents from all ages and backgrounds work towards a more just, peaceful, and inclusive society.
Formal and informal networks of activists; women's groups; civil society leaders; traditional religious and community leaders; local officials; international and regional actors.

Specific objectives: 1) The women’s movement is more inclusive for creating social change; 2) Traditional gender norms are challenged by new gender values, behaviors, and practices; 3) Women’s participation is more diverse and legitimate in peacebuilding.
This programme focusses on cross country and international activities. It is part of a broader international programme implemented by a coalition of NGOs lead by PAX.

comment.narrative: Currently there is minimal awareness / exchange about the context and ongoing activities between the countries and between activists in both – and no perception of what collaboration / sharing can lead to. Many activists are currently operating on a very localized basis.

Descriptions of unique cases in which women's activists expressed solidarity with each other through cross-country collaborations and knowledge-sharing on basis of reciprocity, including rating of relevance / plausible contribution

During an online WPS side-event in 2021, panelists expressed solidarity through collaborative lobbying and public knowledge sharing. 2022: 33 young women activists met up in person in Beirut for a 4-day activist exchange in which they shared experiences and knowledge; deepened their understanding of inclusive movement building and built trust for future collaboration.

title.narrative: 3: Women’s participation is more diverse and legitimate in all stages of peace-building

# of times that CSOs succeed in creating space for CSO demands and positions on promote women’s meaningful and equal participation and leadership in conflict prevention and peace- and state-building and protecting women’s and girls’ rights in crisis and (post-)conflict situations, through agenda setting, influencing the debate and/or movement building

comment.narrative: This component was hardly visible from the perspective of people interviewed. Only well-established activists – with existing experience of participation in international events / negotiations – mentioned and valued this aspect. Some activists recalled that operations from abroad / with the support of international networks were the main avenue for engagement in formal peacebuilding. Training received was also mostly outside the country.

Bottom-up strategic process results in cross-country co-owned lobby and advocacy activities that are relevant, influential and based on strong strategic analysis and positioning at an international level.

In 2021, the consortium co-organized a well-attended side-event during the UNSC Open Debate on WPS, together with the Government of Costa Rica and Sweden, CANVAS, Wo=Men and Oxfam. The side-event highlighted the role of women’s leadership in keeping non-violent discipline, enabling more democratic transitions and their overall success. The side event managed to directly connect to the theme of the Open Debate, and focus on the protection of Women Human Rights Defenders. 2022: During the PAX Peace Week in September 2022, at the Night of Peace event, two peace activists/consortium staff members discussed the important role of women in peacebuilding and what it takes to increase women's political power from a feminist perspective. During the NAP1325 bi-annually signatory event two peace activists joined a hybrid fringe event on the role of women's leadership within non-violent civic resistance and action.

title.narrative: 2: Traditional gender norms are challenged by new gender values, behaviors and practices

comment.narrative: When looking at how to involve activists in political change, awareness raising and outreach can be seen as “the first step of campaigning”. Other than this, there is still relatively little to say: the communication strategy is just starting to shape up. And precise asks / demands will emerge as narratives are generated
Description of unique cases in which gender roles, norms and relations were collaboratively challenged and harvested outcomes indicate initial transformative behavioural changes.

2022: Utilizing a growing number of followers of the program's Facebook, Twitter and Instagram, a coordinated 16-days of activism campaign took place in November 2022 demanding political action to prevent gender based violence and bring perpetrators to justice, while providing sufficient and appropriate care for survivors.
